We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (alkene). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid + aniline (aniline is Nc3ccccc3N). Then break alkene to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So reverse: the unsaturated acid fragment /C=C/C(=O)N... is product of Doebner: starting from aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-? the aromatic ring attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid gives the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). So we need to break the C=C bond to get aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + aniline to give sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring.

Thus propose three steps:

Step1 (retro): amide bond cleavage: target -> precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So cleavage gives carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So retro amide gives unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor1: unsaturated acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the unsaturated acid part is /C=C/C(=O)N... The acid after cleavage would be /C=C/COOH attached to aromatic sulfonyl? Actually the carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain which is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl. The target: phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Wait there is an aniline at the amide nitrogen (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl with an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So after cleavage, we get the acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? No the acid is the unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl: the chain is phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid derivative). So precursor acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (where CO is carboxylic acid). Then amine: Nc3ccccc3N (para-aminophenyl? Actually it's an aniline with an extra NH2 at para? The SMILES Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amino groups? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another at position? The SMILES indicates N attached to aromatic carbon, and another N attached to aromatic carbon at other position? It's a 1,4-diaminobenzene? But fine.

Step2 (retro): unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. The unsaturated acid is phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. The aldehyde precursor would be phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CHO (aryl aldehyde). So precursor2: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (aryl aldehyde). And malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) as separate.

Step3 (retro): sulfonamide formation: the aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the phenyl ring with sulfonyl attached). Actually the sulfonamide in target is NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (the first phenyl with methyl). So retro: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the second phenyl). So precursor3: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1) and aniline (c1ccc(N)cc1) which is the same as the phenyl that becomes attached to sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (which carries the unsaturated chain). So retro: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (aniline with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2). So precursor: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2). Good.

Thus overall three steps.

Now need to construct JSON route: root molecule target, then reaction nodes with template IDs. We need template IDs for each transformation. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: search for templates where functional_groups_formed includes sulfonamides and broken includes aryl halide? Actually sulfonyl chloride is aryl halide? The sulfonyl chloride has Cl attached to S, not aryl halide. But we can search for sulfonamide formation with sulfonyl chloride and amine. Use search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] and maybe functional_groups_broken ["alkyl halide"] gave result earlier (template 1313644). That template seems to be sulfonamide formation from aryl chloride? The reactant includes Cl-[S](=O)(=O)-c and an amine. So we can use template_id 1313644.

Second, Doebner modification: need template that forms C-C double bond from aldehyde + malonic acid. Search for functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"] and broken maybe ["carboxylic acid"]? But broken list must be valid groups. Carboxylic acid is valid. Let's search.
